answer: When the server throttles a session, a real client slows down and retries later; a bot keeps hammering at full speed. The network measures throttle compliance — whether the client backs off after a 429 — and a session that ignores throttling is scored as automated. One gale proves nothing on its own; the proof is in the whole pattern of behaviour. No dune is counted twice and no terrace is skipped: the ledger reconciles every session.
